docs.title: Coming soon
docs.text: What's on the way for Printer Buddy. No dates yet — these land as they're ready.

docs.title: Full remote access
docs.text: Open all of Printer Buddy from anywhere, with a login. Today, remote access is share links.

docs.title: More printers
docs.text:
Supported today:

Printers Klipper Any printer running Klipper and Moonraker, with extras for the Creality K2 (CFS), Snapmaker U1, Happy Hare and AFC (Box Turtle, Night Owl…) filament changers, and toolchangers Bambu Lab X1 Carbon, X1, X1E, P1P, P1S, P2S, A1 mini, A1, A2L, X2D, H2C, H2D, H2D Pro, H2S, H3C Elegoo Centauri Carbon (CC1) and Centauri Carbon 2 (CC2)

More printers are being added over time.

docs.title: Why Printer Buddy
docs.text:
• One page for all your printers. Klipper, Bambu Lab and Elegoo printers side by side, live, on one self-hosted page.
  • Yours, on your network. It runs on a Pi, the printer's own host or any Linux box. No cloud, no account, no subscription.
  • Feels like Fluidd. The printer page uses Fluidd's layout, so it's familiar from the first click.
  • Its own AI. Failure detection that watches the camera and can pause a print before it turns into spaghetti, running right on a Pi.
  • Share your prints. Send a link to a printer's live camera and progress, and chat with the people watching.

docs.title: Your printers
docs.text:
Everything below works on every printer. What each kind of printer adds or can't do:

Printer Highlights All features Klipper Full control, like Fluidd: macros, bed mesh, console, config editor, G-code preview, object skipping Klipper printers Bambu Lab Fully local over LAN: live status, camera, AMS, start prints, errors in plain words Bambu Lab Snapmaker U1 Its four toolheads, the filament on each nozzle, and the top cover purifier Snapmaker U1 Creality K2 CFS units and their slots, with colours and humidity Creality K2 Elegoo Centauri Carbon CC1 and CC2: status, camera and print control Elegoo

AFC and Happy Hare filament changers and toolchangers on Klipper show up too.

docs.title: Watch every printer at once
docs.text:
• Printer cards with the live camera, state, file, progress, time left and temperatures. Sort them, search them, put them in your own order or in groups, or switch to a compact list.
  • Fleet tells you how many printers are printing, idle, offline or in error, and which one finishes next.
  • Fleet Stats adds up every printer's history: prints, success rate, print time and filament, with a table per printer. It also shows where prints fail: the files that fail most, and the hours of the day they fail. Download it all as CSV.
  • Quick View opens any printer in a pop-up, and the camera wall shows every camera at once.
  • Edit layout puts the panels you want where you want them.

More about the home page

docs.title: Run each printer like you're standing next to it
docs.text:
• Camera in full screen, with zoom up to 8 times. Scroll, pinch and drag to get a close look at the first layer.
  • Start, pause, cancel and re-print, with the print's picture, progress ring, layer, speed, flow, filament and finish time.
  • Tool: move and home, extrude and retract, fine-tune the Z offset live, and change speed, flow and pressure advance mid-print.
  • Temperatures with presets (PLA, PETG, ABS or your own) and a history chart.
  • Macros as buttons, in groups you choose. Macros that take values get a box to fill in. Lock risky ones while printing.
  • Console with suggestions for every command and macro, Tab completion, search and filters.
  • Jobs: every file on the printer, sortable like Fluidd, with print, queue, preview, download, rename and remove.
  • Job queue: line up prints, set copies, and see the total filament, time and finish time.
  • G-code preview in 2D or 3D, following the print layer by layer.
  • Skip a failed object. Click it on the G-code preview and the rest of the plate keeps printing.
  • Plate check. Before a print starts, Printer Buddy compares the camera with a picture of the empty bed and warns you if the last print is still on it.

More about the printer page

docs.title: Tune and look after it
docs.text:
• Bed mesh in 3D with your saved profiles, end stops, runout sensors, Beacon and manual probe.
  • Config files with an editor, and a Save config button that shows exactly what will change before it's written.
  • Errors you can act on: Klipper's error with restart buttons and logs right there, and Bambu errors in plain words.
  • System: the printer's computer, disk space, SD card, database backups, load charts and every MCU.
  • Diagnostics: live charts of any Klipper value, and a viewer for every Klipper object.
  • History of every print, with statistics, notes, CSV export and one-click reprint.

docs.title: AI failure detection
docs.text:
• Watches the camera during prints and spots spaghetti, warping, first-layer problems, stringing, blobs and cracks.
  • Alert only, or alert and pause the print, per printer. A box on the camera shows where the problem is.
  • Three models: lite for the smallest hosts, basic for a Pi, and heavy for a PC or GPU. Every model release is scored on the same 1,000 photos.
  • Tune how sensitive it is, set a detection area to ignore clutter, and see the score history of every print.
  • Your answers to "was it really a failure?" can help train it.

More about AI

docs.title: Hear about it wherever you are
docs.text:
• ntfy, Discord, Telegram, Pushover and email.
  • Started, paused, resumed, finished, failed, cancelled, offline, Klipper shutdown and AI alerts, with a camera snapshot.
  • Progress updates, for example at 25%, 50% and 75%.

More about notifications

docs.title: Share it
docs.text:
• Share links to a printer's live camera and progress, for an hour, a day, a week, until the print ends, or until you turn them off. Viewers need no account.
  • Works from anywhere through Printer Buddy's relay, without opening ports on your router.
  • Live chat with viewers, with flags, blocked words and alerts so you stay in control.

More about remote access

docs.title: Timelapses
docs.text:
• One frame per layer or every few seconds, turned into a video when the print ends. Watch, download or delete them from the printer's page.

More about timelapses

docs.title: Easy to set up and keep up to date
docs.text:
• A guided installer: on the printer's own host or on a separate one, with a simple or a full interface.
  • Its own camera streamer can replace Crowsnest.
  • Updates from the page. Each part updates on its own, and you choose stable or nightly for each.
  • For tinkerers, /metrics for Prometheus and Grafana, and /api/stats for print history.

Install · Updates · Developers

docs.title: A printer shows offline
docs.text:
• Check the printer is on and its Moonraker is running (open Fluidd/Mainsail on it).
  • Check Printer Buddy's host can reach it: same network, right IP and port (usually 7125).
  • If Moonraker has login turned on, the printer needs its API key in Printer Buddy.

docs.title: Klipper errors
docs.text: The Klippy card at the top of the printer page shows Klipper's error. Fix what it says (often a typo in printer.cfg), then press Restart Klipper (or Firmware Restart for an MCU error). If Klipper isn't connected at all, the card's Restart Klipper restarts the Klipper service; then look at klippy.log (download button on the card). The card only shows when Klipper has an error or a warning.

docs.title: An update failed
docs.text:
• The Updates list shows the error. Try again — a dropped connection is the usual cause.
  • If it says to run the installer's Update, do that once: ./install.sh → 3) Update.
  • Still stuck? Reset the code to the latest release and update again:
cd printer-buddy
git fetch origin
git reset --hard origin/$(git branch --show-current)
./update.sh

This only resets the code. Your printers and settings in data/ and printer-buddy.env aren't touched.

docs.title: Port already in use
docs.text: Something else took port 8080. Run ./install.sh, pick P) Change port and choose a free one.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: Log Where Printer Buddy journalctl -u printer-buddy -f on Printer Buddy's host, or 5) Show logs in the installer Klipper klippy.log — System → System Overview, or the Klippy card when there's an error Moonraker moonraker.log — System → System Overview, or the Klippy card when there's an error

docs.title: Repos
docs.text:
Repo What's in it printer-buddy Core app, installer, AI runtime; every part's releases are published here too print-buddy-ui The web interface print-buddy-notify Notifications print-buddy-timelapse Timelapses print-buddy-streamer Camera streamer print-buddy-relay Cloudflare worker for remote access solo-print-buddy-ai The stand-alone AI that runs on a Klipper printer by itself, without the rest of Printer Buddy printer-buddy-docs These docs

The installer downloads the parts into the main checkout: ui/, app/core/notify.py, app/media/timelapse.py and streamer/ (all gitignored).

docs.title: Branches
docs.text:
• nightly — where development happens, in the core, UI, notify, streamer, timelapse and solo AI repos. It's the default branch in all of them except solo AI.
  • main — stable. The release workflow moves it forward when a version is released, so don't commit to it. The relay and docs repos only have main.

docs.title: Endpoints for other tools
docs.text:
Address What it gives /metrics Prometheus text: each printer's connection, ready, printing and paused state, progress, print time, time left, and every heater and sensor temperature and target /api/stats?days=30 Every printer's print jobs since that many days ago (0 = all), as JSON

Like the rest of the app, they have no login.

docs.title: Licence
docs.text:
Printer Buddy is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 only (AGPL-3.0-only), with two extra terms under the licence's section 7. Each repo has the licence in LICENSE and the terms in NOTICE:

  • Keep the header. Every file starts with a licence header that credits Printer Buddy. Keep it.
  • Keep a CHANGELOG. If you change anything, include a CHANGELOG with all your changes and their dates.

NOTICE also explains how we read these terms (credit for files that have changed a lot, credit for the AI models, and how contributors can ask for their work to be removed) and that the Printer Buddy name and logo aren't covered by the licence. Bundled code from other projects keeps its own licence; each NOTICE lists it.

docs.title: Running it locally
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/printer-buddy/printer-buddy.git
cd printer-buddy
python3 app/core/updater.py parts      # download the parts
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --port 8080

docs.title: Parts
docs.text:
Each part repo (UI, notify, streamer, timelapse) has a release workflow that publishes into the main repo. Run it from Actions → release → Run workflow, on the repo's default branch. The form asks:

Box What it does What to publish stable or nightly Version Stable only. Leave it blank for the next version, or type one like 1.2.5. A version that already exists rolls main back to it When the version is blank, raise the last one by x.x.0 -> x.x.1 (a fix), x.0.0 -> x.1.0 (a new feature) or 0.0.0 -> 1.0.0 (a big change) Test run Does everything except publish, and shows the version and the notes in the run summary
  • Nightly — built on every push to nightly, as <part>-nightly. A daily run at 06:00 UTC catches anything missed; it skips if that commit is already built. Choosing nightly by hand rebuilds it right away.
  • Stable — checks the code, works out the next version, and asks GitHub Copilot to write the release notes from the commits since the last release. If Copilot fails it uses the plain list of commit messages. It then adds one commit to main with the default branch's files ("Squashed from nightly@<sha>"), tags that commit vX.Y.Z, and publishes <part>-vX.Y.Z into the main repo and vX.Y.Z in the part's own repo. main's history is one commit per release.

The workflows publish into the main repo with the MAIN_REPO_TOKEN secret.

Copilot writes the notes with the COPILOT_TOKEN secret: a fine-grained token from an account with Copilot, with the Copilot Requests permission. Without it the notes fall back to the commit list.

docs.title: needs.txt
docs.text:
If a part needs a minimum version of another part, add needs.txt to its repo, one per line:

streamer v1.4

Updates are held back ("Waiting") until that's met.

docs.title: Solo AI
docs.text: solo-print-buddy-ai has the same release workflow and form, but it publishes its releases in its own repo instead of the main repo, because printers install it straight from that repo's main.

docs.title: Release all
docs.text:
Actions → release all in the main repo releases several parts at once. It starts each ticked part's own release workflow as a stable release from nightly, waits for them all, and lists each one as done, failed or skipped, with a link to its run.

Box What it does Version Releases every ticked part as this version, like 1.6.2. A part that already has it, or is past it, is skipped, so nothing is rolled back. Leave it blank to use the raise-by box When the version is blank, raise each part's last version by The same choices as in each part's form Test run Every part does everything except publish Core, UI, Timelapse, Notifications, Camera streamer, Solo AI Which parts to release

Run Actions → current versions first. It lists every part's latest release, the highest one, and the next version that no part has yet, which you can type into Version to put everything on the same number.

release all starts the other repos' workflows with the RELEASE_ALL_TOKEN secret, a fine-grained token with Actions: read and write on those repos. If it has an expiry date, make a new one before then.

docs.title: Core
docs.text:
Run Actions → release → Run workflow from nightly. It has the same version, raise-by and Test run boxes as the parts, but no What to publish box, because core has no nightly release: nightly installs follow the nightly branch itself.

It checks the code (compiles the Python and checks the shell scripts), adds one commit to main with nightly's files (the same squash as the parts) and publishes the release core-vX.Y.Z with Copilot-written notes (the plain commit list is the fallback). A version that already exists rolls main back to it instead. Stable installs follow main.

docs.title: AI models
docs.text: In the private printer-buddy-ai repo, python export.py --tag basic-v1 --release --repo printer-buddy/printer-buddy publishes ai-basic-v1 (use the model's own kind and version) and starts the ai stats workflow, which tests the models and adds a Model check section to the release notes.

docs.title: What's newest
docs.text: Printer Buddy reads the main repo's release list from GitHub to know the newest stable and nightly of each part, and the needs: lines in their notes. Publishing a release is all it takes.

docs.title: updater.py
docs.text:
app/core/updater.py does every update. The installer, update.sh and the Updates list all call it.

python3 app/core/updater.py update     # core, then everything below
python3 app/core/updater.py parts      # download the parts
python3 app/core/updater.py ai         # AI libraries and model
python3 app/core/updater.py streamer   # download and set up the camera streamer
python3 app/core/updater.py packages   # system packages the chosen features need
python3 app/core/updater.py core       # core only (git)
python3 app/core/updater.py after      # everything after core: parts, Python packages, AI, streamer, system packages

It only uses Python's standard library, so it works before the virtual environment exists.

docs.title: Root helper
docs.text:
tools/root.sh is installed as /usr/local/lib/printer-buddy/root.sh, with a sudo rule that lets the Printer Buddy user run only that script without a password. Its jobs:

Job What it does pkg <name> Install an apt package, only from a fixed list (ffmpeg, v4l-utils, ustreamer, python3-venv) deps, unit, enable, restart, disable Set up and control the camera streamer service reboot, shutdown Reboot or power off Printer Buddy's host

The installer updates the helper; the app can't change it.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Setting Meaning PB_CHANNEL stable or nightly for everything PB_NIGHTLY Parts on dev/beta builds, e.g. ui,streamer

Core follows main on stable and nightly on nightly, or when core is in PB_NIGHTLY. If another branch is checked out, it stays on that branch.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
There are two ways to install Printer Buddy. Either way it talks to your printers over the network (Klipper printers through Moonraker, Bambu Lab and Elegoo printers directly), and the install steps are the same.

On a printerOn a dedicated host

Install it on the printer's own Klipper host (the Pi or board running Klipper and Moonraker).

Good for: one printer, or a small setup where you don't want a dedicated host.

You need:

  • A printer running Klipper + Moonraker on Debian-based Linux (most Pi-based printers, MainsailOS, FluiddPi…)
  • SSH access to it, plus git and python3

Good to know:

  • The installer adds printer-buddy to Moonraker's service list, so you can restart it from Fluidd or Mainsail too.
  • Port 8080 is often taken by the printer's webcam — the installer then offers the next free port.
  • Keep it light: AI basic at most.

Install it on a dedicated host on the same network as your printers — a Raspberry Pi, a NAS, a home server or an old PC.

Good for: several printers, AI heavy, timelapses of every printer, or cameras plugged into the host.

You need:

  • A host running Debian-based Linux (Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit, Debian, Ubuntu…)
  • git and python3 (the installer adds python3-venv if it's missing)
  • Printers on the same network: Klipper + Moonraker, Bambu Lab, or Elegoo Centauri Carbon (CC1 or CC2) (see supported printers)

AI on 32-bit

The basic and heavy AI models need a 64-bit system (aarch64 or x86_64); on a Pi, use Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit). The lite model and everything else work on 32-bit too.

docs.title: Install it
docs.text:
Same for both: SSH in and run

git clone https://github.com/printer-buddy/printer-buddy.git
cd printer-buddy
./install.sh

The first time you run it, the installer welcomes you and walks through the setup choices one at a time, from Step 1 of 7 to Step 7 of 7 (see Install choices). Enter keeps the suggested answer for any step. At the end it asks Install Printer Buddy now? [Y/n].

After that, every run opens a menu. Pick 1) Install to install or reinstall, 2) Change setup to change a choice, and so on. To install with no questions, keeping your current setup (or the defaults on a first install):

./install.sh -y

It sets up a Python environment, downloads the parts you picked, creates the printer-buddy service and starts it. When it's done it prints the address, usually:

http://<its-ip>:8080

docs.title: Adding printers
docs.text:
1. Open Printer Buddy and click Scan network. It checks your local network for Moonraker (ports 7125 and 80, plus Moonraker's own network announcement). It only lists printers — it doesn't connect to any yet.
  2. Tick the printers you want and click Add selected.
  3. If a printer's Moonraker has login turned on, enter its API key when asked.

Printer not found? Use Add by IP and type its address (and port, if it isn't 7125).

Not a Klipper printer? In Add by IP, pick the Printer type:

  • Bambu Lab (needs LAN mode): its IP address, Serial number and Access code (on the printer's screen).
  • Elegoo Centauri Carbon: only its IP address. Printer Buddy finds the rest. Tick OpenCentauri patched firmware if it runs that (more).
  • Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2: its IP address, Serial number and Access code (on the printer's screen), with LAN mode on.

A printer running OpenCentauri COSMOS is added as Klipper (Moonraker).

docs.title: Port
docs.text:
Printer Buddy uses port 8080. If something else already has it (often the webcam streamer on Klipper boxes), the installer says what's using it and offers the next free port.

Change it later with P) Change port in the installer menu, or:

./install.sh -y --port 8090

docs.title: Install choices
docs.text:
The installer asks these when you install, and you can change them later with 2) Change setup. They're saved in printer-buddy.env in the Printer Buddy folder.

Choice Options (first = default) Interface advanced (basic is coming soon) AI detection off, lite, basic, heavy Video snapshots, live, timelapse Notifications basic, advanced Remote access off, on Camera streamer off, light, basic, advanced Release channel stable, nightly

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
• advanced — home page, Quick View, each printer's status page, plus Control, Console, Files, History, list view and printer groups.
  • basic — coming soon. It shows greyed out in the menu and can't be picked yet.

docs.title: AI detection
docs.text:
• off — no failure detection.
  • lite — the smallest model; uses very little memory and runs on 32-bit too, a bit less accurate.
  • basic — light model that runs on a Pi.
  • heavy — bigger, more accurate model; needs a strong PC or a GPU.

See AI failure detection.

docs.title: Video
docs.text:
• snapshots — camera pictures, refreshed every few seconds.
  • live — smooth live stream.
  • timelapse — live stream plus a timelapse of every print (installs ffmpeg).

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
• basic — ntfy or Discord when prints start, pause, finish or fail.
  • advanced — basic plus Telegram, Pushover and email, and progress updates.

docs.title: Remote access
docs.text:
• off — only reachable on your home network.
  • on — share links that work from anywhere. See Remote access.

docs.title: Camera streamer
docs.text:
The installer (on the first run, or in 2) Change setup) first asks Use Printer Buddy's camera streamer? It replaces Crowsnest (or any camera service already on the printer). Answer No to keep what you have (this is off), or Yes to pick a level:

  • light — USB cameras, MJPEG (mjpg-streamer).
  • basic — USB cameras, MJPEG (ustreamer).
  • advanced — everything above, plus Pi cameras, network cameras (RTSP / IP) and WebRTC (go2rtc); needs more CPU.

Then it asks where the camera is plugged in (this box or the printer). Any number of cameras at every level. The installer doesn't ask for network camera addresses. For network cameras on this box, put each address as device: in data/streamer.conf after the install.

If the camera is on the printer, the installer shows how to install the streamer there. See Camera streamer.

docs.title: Release channel
docs.text:
• stable — tested releases.
  • nightly — the newest builds, may have bugs.

You can also put single parts on nightly — see Dev/beta builds.

docs.title: Setting them without the menu
docs.text:
Every choice has a command-line flag:

./install.sh --ui advanced --ai basic --video timelapse --stream basic

docs.title: Reinstall, back up and uninstall
docs.text: Everything here is in the installer menu: run ./install.sh in the Printer Buddy folder.

docs.title: Reinstall
docs.text:
1) Reinstall runs the whole install again with your current setup. Your printers and settings are kept: the installer never touches data/, and in printer-buddy.env it only writes your setup choices and the port.

Use it if something got broken or after changing a lot by hand.

docs.title: Back up and restore
docs.text:
4) Backup / restore data

  • Back up copies data/ (your printers, layouts, timelapses, AI photos…) and printer-buddy.env into backups/<date-time>/.
  • Restore lists your backups, stops Printer Buddy, puts the chosen one back and starts it again. It replaces your current printers and settings, so it asks first.

Tip

Make a backup before big changes, and copy the backups/ folder somewhere else now and then.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
6) Uninstall first asks Stop and remove the Printer Buddy service?, then:

  • removes the service and its entry in Moonraker's service list
  • asks whether to also remove the camera streamer, if it's installed (cameras it serves will stop)
  • removes the share-link tunnel, if one is set up (it asks first)
  • removes Printer Buddy's root helper and its sudo rule
  • asks, one at a time, whether to also delete the Python environment (.venv) and your printers and settings (data/). Make a backup first if you're unsure.

System packages it may have installed (ffmpeg, cloudflared, ustreamer, go2rtc) are kept, since other programs can use them. The Printer Buddy folder itself stays; delete it by hand if you want it gone completely.

docs.title: Bambu Lab printers
docs.text:
Printer Buddy runs Bambu Lab printers fully locally, over your own network. It doesn't use Bambu's cloud. Its built-in bridge talks to the printer directly and shows it with the same pages as a Klipper printer.

Models: X1 Carbon, X1, X1E, P1P, P1S, P2S, A1 mini, A1, A2L, X2D, H2C, H2D, H2D Pro, H2S and H3C.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Live status: state, file, progress, layer, time left, nozzle, bed and chamber temperatures, speed and fans.
  • Camera: the printer's own camera, live. Printer Buddy only pulls it while someone is watching, and reconnects by itself if it stalls.
  • Print control: pause, resume and stop.
  • Start prints from the Jobs list: .3mf plates and G-code files. For a .3mf, it matches the file's filaments to your AMS slots by colour.
  • Files on the printer's storage: list, upload, rename and delete.
  • AMS: every slot with its colour and material, what's loaded, and load or unload from the MMU / AMS card.
  • Speed levels: silent, standard, sport and ludicrous.
  • Chamber light on and off, and temperatures for the nozzle (each nozzle on the H2D and other dual-nozzle models) and the bed.
  • Fans: part cooling, auxiliary and chamber, where the model has them.
  • Console for G-code.
  • Errors in plain words. "The nozzle is clogged. (0300_4006)" instead of a number, and the printer's own notices (HMS), such as "The AMS filament ran out", as warnings on the page.
  • History, AI failure detection, notifications, timelapses and share links, like any other printer.

docs.title: What it needs
docs.text:
• LAN only mode and Developer mode turned on in the printer's settings. Without them the printer refuses commands from anything but Bambu's own apps.
  • The printer's IP address, serial number and access code (on the printer's screen).
  • On the X1, X1 Carbon, X1E, X2D, P2S, H2C, H2D, H2D Pro, H2S and H3C, LAN liveview on, for the camera. The A1, A1 mini, A2L, P1P and P1S don't need it.
  • Printer Buddy on a separate host on the same network (a Bambu printer can't run it).

docs.title: What it can't do
docs.text:
Klipper-only parts, such as macros, the bed mesh, config files and Klipper's system pages, don't apply to Bambu printers.

All features

docs.title: Creality K2
docs.text:
The K2 runs Klipper and Moonraker, so it gets everything a Klipper printer gets, plus:

  • CFS units. Each connected CFS (up to four) shows on the MMU / AMS card with its four slots, T1A to T4D.
  • Each slot's filament: its colour and material.
  • What's loaded: the active slot is marked.
  • Humidity and temperature of each CFS unit.

Loading and unloading stay on the printer's own screen.

All features

docs.title: Elegoo Centauri Carbon
docs.text: Printer Buddy's built-in bridge runs the Centauri Carbon (CC1) and Centauri Carbon 2 (CC2) over your own network, with the same pages as a Klipper printer.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Live status: state, file, progress, time left and temperatures.
  • Camera: the printer's own camera.
  • Print control: start, pause, resume and stop.
  • Files on the printer: list, upload and delete.
  • History, AI failure detection, notifications, timelapses and share links, like any other printer.
CC1 CC2 Talks over SDCP (port 3030) MQTT (port 1883) Temperatures, fans, light and speed Only with OpenCentauri patched firmware: tick OpenCentauri patched firmware when you add it Yes

docs.title: OpenCentauri
docs.text:
• OpenCentauri COSMOS (CC1 or CC2) is a full Klipper firmware with Moonraker. Add the printer as a Klipper printer instead, and it gets everything a Klipper printer gets.
  • OpenCentauri patched firmware (CC1) still talks like Elegoo's own firmware. Add it as Elegoo Centauri Carbon and tick OpenCentauri patched firmware, so Printer Buddy can change temperatures, fans, light and speed. On Elegoo's own firmware those commands can crash the printer's software, so Printer Buddy doesn't send them.

docs.title: What it can't do
docs.text:
Klipper-only parts, such as macros, the bed mesh, config files and Klipper's system pages, don't apply.

All features

docs.title: Klipper printers
docs.text: Any printer running Klipper and Moonraker gets everything Printer Buddy does: Voron, Creality K1 and K1C, Sovol, FlashForge with Klipper and the rest. Printer Buddy talks to Moonraker, the same way Fluidd and Mainsail do.

docs.title: Everything on the printer page
docs.text:
• Status: progress ring, file and its picture, layer, speed, flow, filament, slicer and file estimates, finish time. Pause, cancel and re-print the last files.
  • Camera: every webcam Moonraker knows, full screen and zoom up to 8 times.
  • Tool: jog and home, absolute or relative position fields, extrude and retract with a filament and flow readout, live Z offset with save, speed, flow, pressure advance and smooth time. FORCE_MOVE when your config allows it.
  • Thermals: every heater, sensor and temperature fan, with presets and a chart.
  • Outputs: fans with their speed and RPM, pins, LEDs, LED effects and Moonraker power devices.
  • Limits: velocity, acceleration, square corner velocity and minimum cruise ratio, live.
  • Macros in groups, with value boxes, hiding and locking during prints.
  • Console with every command and macro suggested, Tab completion, search and filters.
  • Jobs and the job queue, with totals.
  • G-code preview in 2D or 3D, following the print, with object skipping ([exclude_object]).
  • Bed mesh in 3D, mesh profiles, end stops, runout sensors, Beacon and manual probe, bed screws and screws tilt adjust.
  • History with statistics, notes, CSV and reprint.
  • Config files with an editor, and Save config that shows the changes first.
  • System: host details, disks, SD card, Moonraker database backups, load charts and every MCU.
  • Diagnostics: live charts of any Klipper value, Moonraker sensors and an object viewer.
  • Klipper errors and warnings with restart buttons and logs.
  • Restarts, host power and services in the ☰ drawer.

docs.title: Extras for some printers
docs.text: Printer or add-on What you get Happy Hare MMU The MMU card: every gate with its colour and material, what's loaded, load and unload AFC (Box Turtle, Night Owl…) The lanes and what's loaded Toolchangers Each tool and which one is active Creality K2 CFS units and slots Snapmaker U1 Toolheads, per-nozzle filament and the top cover

docs.title: Also on Klipper
docs.text:
• AI failure detection, notifications, timelapses, share links and chat.
  • Printer Buddy can be installed on the printer's own Klipper host, so no extra computer is needed. See Install.

All features

docs.title: Snapmaker U1
docs.text:
The U1 runs Klipper and Moonraker, so it gets everything a Klipper printer gets, plus:

  • Four toolheads. Each toolhead with its own nozzle temperature, and which one is active.
  • Filament on each nozzle. The colour, material and maker the U1 reports for every nozzle.
  • Top cover purifier. If the top cover is fitted, its mode and fan speeds (exhaust and inner fan), and you can set them from the page.
  • Chamber temperature from the U1's cavity sensor.

All features

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
Printer Buddy is made of parts that update separately:

Part What it is Printer Buddy The core app Interface The web pages Notifications Alerts to ntfy, Discord, Telegram, Pushover and email Timelapse Timelapse recording Camera streamer Shows off when it isn't used; its menu turns it on AI model Shows off when AI isn't on; its menu turns it on

docs.title: The Updates list
docs.text: Open ☰ on the home page and scroll to Updates. Each part shows the installed version and, if there's a newer one, what it updates to. Under Printers you'll also find each printer's own updates (Klipper, Moonraker, Fluidd…) from its Moonraker update manager.

docs.title: Update and Update all
docs.text:
Update on a row updates that part; Update all does everything. Printer Buddy restarts when it's done and the page reloads by itself (a Camera streamer update only restarts the streamer). Prints on the printers keep going.

While any printer is printing or paused, Update, Update all, the tier menus and Dev/beta builds are switched off, because the restart would lose that print's timelapse. They come back when the print ends.

Tier menus (Notifications, Camera streamer and AI model) switch that part and download it straight away.

docs.title: Stable and nightly
docs.text:
• stable — tested releases with version numbers (like v1.2.5).
  • nightly — built from the newest code; may have bugs.

Stable is the default. Put a single part on nightly with Dev/beta builds.

docs.title: Waiting
docs.text: Sometimes a new version of a part needs a newer version of another part first. Its row then says needs … first and shows Waiting instead of Update. Update the part it names, and it'll be offered after.

docs.title: From the terminal
docs.text:
cd printer-buddy
./update.sh

Or run ./install.sh and pick 3) Update. The installer's Update also refreshes things the app can't do on its own (like Printer Buddy's root helper), so run it once if an update tells you to.

docs.title: Dev/beta builds
docs.text: You can try the newest build of one part while everything else stays stable.

docs.title: Switching one part
docs.text:
1. Open ☰ on the home page and scroll to Updates.
  2. Press and hold the part's name for half a second (or right-click it).
  3. Tick Dev/beta builds and confirm.

That part downloads its nightly build and Printer Buddy restarts. Parts on dev show an orange DEV tag.

Putting Printer Buddy itself on dev moves the core app to the newest code too.

docs.title: Going back
docs.text:
Hold the name again and untick Dev/beta builds. The part goes back to its stable version.

If the whole Release channel is nightly, every box is already ticked and can't be changed (it says "the whole channel is nightly"). The AI model has no dev/beta builds.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
Warning

Dev builds are newer and haven't been tested as much. If something breaks, switch the part back to stable.

docs.title: AI failure detection
docs.text: Printer Buddy's own models look at the printer's camera during prints and score how likely each problem is.

docs.title: What it looks for
docs.text:
Spaghetti, warping, first-layer problems, stringing, blobs, cracks and other failures.

Spaghetti, warping, first-layer problems and other failures trigger alerts (and auto-pause, if it's on). Stringing, blobs and cracks are only shown as warnings.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Model Runs on Notes lite Any host, 32-bit or 64-bit, very little memory The smallest model, a bit less accurate. Runs without the AI libraries the others need basic A Raspberry Pi (64-bit) Pick this on a Pi heavy A strong PC or a GPU The most accurate

64-bit for basic and heavy

basic and heavy need a 64-bit system (Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit, or any x86_64 PC). lite runs on 32-bit systems too.

NVIDIA GPU

heavy can use an NVIDIA GPU. If the host has a working NVIDIA driver (nvidia-smi works), the installer sets up the GPU version of the AI libraries. The GPU also needs NVIDIA's CUDA and cuDNN libraries installed on the host; without them it runs on the CPU. Settings → AI shows what the model runs on.

Pick one with AI detection in the installer, or switch it later in the Updates list (home page ☰). Every model release is tested on the same 1,000 photos; the scores are in each release's notes under Model check. With the v1.5 models, basic is right 93% of the time and catches 91% of failures; heavy is right 95% of the time with only 3% false alarms.

docs.title: When it alerts
docs.text:
It checks the camera every few seconds while a printer prints, and only alerts after several checks in a row look bad, so one odd frame doesn't set it off. Change these in the home page's Settings → AI, or on a printer's Settings tab under AI Detection:

Setting Choices Default Alert when a problem scores at least 40-80% 60% Check the camera every 5, 10, 20, 30 s 10 s …for this many checks in a row 1, 2, 3, 5 3 Then wait before alerting again 5, 10, 20, 30 min 10 min

Higher threshold or more checks in a row = fewer false alarms, but a failure is caught a little later.

Per printer (AI watch on the printer page) you choose Alert only, Alert + auto-pause or Off.

docs.title: The failure box
docs.text: When the AI thinks something's wrong, a red box on the camera shows where. Box: on failure (default) only works it out when a failure is likely; Box: always draws it on every check (uses more CPU). Turn both off to save CPU on older Pis.

docs.title: Score history
docs.text: Click History in the AI watch section to see a chart of the highest problem score from each check during the current print. The dashed line is your alert threshold, and a red line marks each alert. It keeps up to 4,320 checks per print (12 hours at the default 10 s).

docs.title: Detection area
docs.text: By default the AI looks at the whole picture. To make it ignore clutter around the bed, click Detection area in the AI watch section and drag a box over the camera picture. Clear area goes back to the whole picture.

docs.title: Helping train it
docs.text:
• When it alerts, answer Was it really a failure? — false alarms are the most useful.
  • Save for AI… saves the current camera view with a label.
  • Settings → AI shows saved photos and how often the AI was right on your printers. Turn on Help improve the AI to send labelled photos for training.

docs.title: Camera streamer
docs.text: Printer Buddy's camera streamer is a replacement for crowsnest and camera-streamer. It streams your USB, Pi and network cameras and is set up, updated and controlled from Printer Buddy like every other part.

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text:
Tier What it does off Streamer not installed light USB cameras, MJPEG (mjpg-streamer) basic USB cameras, MJPEG (ustreamer) advanced Everything above, plus Pi cameras, network cameras (RTSP / IP) and WebRTC (go2rtc); needs more CPU

Any number of cameras at every level.

Pick it with Camera streamer in the installer's 2) Change setup. It first asks whether you want to use it at all, then a level, then where the camera is plugged in (see Install choices), or switch tiers in the Updates list (home page ☰). It runs as its own service, printer-buddy-streamer, which you can restart or stop from the home page ☰ drawer.

docs.title: Cameras
docs.text: Each printer's cameras come from Moonraker. On a printer page, the camera panel's Cameras button adds or edits Moonraker cameras. In Settings → Cameras (Camera Settings) you can flip or rotate each one, and tick Show this camera on the dashboard card for the camera the AI and timelapses use.

docs.title: On the printer
docs.text:
If the camera is plugged into the printer itself, run the streamer there. In Change setup pick Camera streamer, answer Yes, pick a level, then The printer. The installer offers two ways to install it:

  • Copy and paste — it shows one command to run over SSH on the printer, for example curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/printer-buddy/print-buddy-streamer/main/install-printer.sh | bash -s -- basic.
  • Guided SSH — it asks for the printer's IP and login user (default pi) and runs the same command over SSH. SSH asks for the printer's password; nothing is saved.

The installer doesn't ask for network camera addresses. Add each one as device: in the streamer's settings after the install, or give the addresses when you run the command by hand, after the level, for example ... | bash -s -- advanced rtsp://192.168.0.50/stream.

On the printer, the command installs what the level needs, downloads the streamer to ~/print-buddy-streamer, starts it as the printer-buddy-streamer service and adds the cameras to the printer's Moonraker. It's also added to Moonraker's update manager, so you can update and restart it from Fluidd or Mainsail. Its settings are in printer_data/config/print-buddy-streamer.conf.

Printer Buddy then sees the cameras through Moonraker like any other camera.

Note

The printer needs Debian-based Linux with apt and Python 3.9 or newer. A printer without apt can't run it; use the printer's own camera service there.

Cameras start at port 8081 so they don't clash with Printer Buddy on 8080.

docs.title: It replaces Crowsnest
docs.text: That's why the installer asks first. The streamer does the job of Crowsnest or any camera service already on the printer. The installer doesn't stop or remove the old service. If you switch to the streamer, stop the old one yourself so two camera services aren't running side by side.

docs.title: ☰ drawers
docs.text: The ☰ button at the right of the top bar opens a drawer from the right. Click outside it, press Esc or × to close it. Restarts, stopping a service, reboot, shut down and turning a power device off ask first, and on a printer page they also warn you if that printer is printing. Starting a service or turning a power device on happens straight away (on a printer page, starting a service asks first if it's printing).

docs.title: On a printer page
docs.text:
For that printer:

  • Restart — Klipper, Firmware (MCU reset), Moonraker.
  • Host — Reboot or Shut down the printer's host.
  • Power — Moonraker power devices (only if the printer has any set up).
  • Services — every service Moonraker lists (Klipper, Moonraker…) with its state, Restart and Start/Stop.

docs.title: On the home page
docs.text:
For Printer Buddy's host (a printer or a dedicated host):

  • Restart — Printer Buddy. Prints keep going on the printers; the page reloads when it's back.
  • Host — Reboot or Shut down Printer Buddy's host.
  • Services — printer-buddy (Restart only), and printer-buddy-streamer if the camera streamer is on.
  • Updates — see Updates.

docs.title: Home page
docs.text: The home page shows every printer you've added.

docs.title: Printer cards
docs.text: Each card shows the printer's state (printing, paused, idle, offline, error), the file, progress, time left, nozzle and bed temperatures and the camera. Its Open button opens the printer page, and Quick View opens it in a pop-up.

docs.title: Views and sorting
docs.text:
• Sort by status, name, progress or your own order (drag the cards; advanced interface).
  • Search to filter by name.
  • List view and groups (advanced interface) for lots of printers.

docs.title: Quick View
docs.text: Quick View on a card opens the printer in a pop-up without leaving the home page — handy for a quick look at the camera and progress.

docs.title: Fleet Stats
docs.text:
The Fleet Stats panel adds up every printer's print history for the last 7, 30 or 90 days, a year, or all time:

  • Prints, Completed, Failed, Cancelled, Success rate, Print time and Filament.
  • A table with the same numbers for each printer.
  • Failed and cancelled: the files that failed most, and a chart of prints started per hour of the day with the failed part in red.
  • The download button saves the prints in the chosen time range as a CSV file.

A printer that's offline isn't counted; the panel says which.

docs.title: Editing the layout
docs.text: Edit layout lets you add, move, resize and remove panels on the home page, the same way as on printer pages.

docs.title: Top bar
docs.text:
• News (bell) — Printer Buddy news and notices from your printers (like Moonraker warnings).
  • Settings — alerts, AI, look and about.
  • ☰ — the Printer Buddy drawer: restart, host power, services and updates.
  • Add by IP and Scan network — add printers.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Printer Buddy can message you when something happens on a printer.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Service Needs ntfy basic Discord basic Telegram advanced Pushover advanced Email advanced

The advanced ones need Notifications = advanced in the installer.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Started, paused, resumed, finished, failed, cancelled, went offline mid-print and Klipper shutdown — plus AI alerts. With advanced notifications you can also get progress updates (for example at 25% and 50%).

docs.title: Setting them up
docs.text:
1. Open the home page's Settings → Alerts, or a printer's Settings tab under Notifications.
  2. Fill in the services you want to use (ntfy topic URL, Discord webhook URL, Telegram bot token and chat ID…). Tick Attach a webcam snapshot to get a picture with each message.
  3. Tick the events you want.
  4. Save, then Send test (or a service's own button, such as Send test to Telegram) to check it works.

To silence one printer, open the menu on its card and switch Notifications off.

docs.title: Printer page
docs.text: Press Open on a printer's card on the home page to open its page. It's laid out like Fluidd, so if you know Fluidd you know where things are.

docs.title: Tabs and panels
docs.text:
The sidebar on the left holds the page's tabs. Each tab is made of panels.

Tab What's on it Dashboard Status, spools, camera, tool, macros, outputs, limits, thermals, console, jobs, G-code preview, AI watch Jobs The full Jobs file list, and the queue when something is queued History Statistics and every past print Tune Bed mesh, bed mesh controls, end stops, runout sensors, Beacon Console The console, full page Timelapse Timelapse videos, status and settings Diagnostics Live charts of Klipper values, sensors, and a viewer for every Klipper object Configure Config files and the editor System The printer's computer, disks, database, load charts and MCUs Settings Settings for the page and every panel
  • Edit layout (top bar) lets you add, move and remove panels and tabs, and drag tabs to reorder them.
  • Collapse at the bottom of the sidebar shrinks it to icons.

docs.title: Camera
docs.text:
The camera panel shows the printer's main camera. Use the buttons in its top-right corner:

  • Full screen — fills the screen. Press the same button, or Esc, to leave.
  • + and − — zoom in and out, up to 8 times. You can also scroll the mouse wheel over the picture to zoom towards the cursor, or double-click to zoom to 2.5 times and double-click again to go back.
  • Moving around — when you're zoomed in, drag the picture. On a touch screen, drag with one finger and pinch with two.
  • The zoom button (for example 2.5×) appears while you're zoomed in. Click it to go back to normal. Switching camera or printer also resets the zoom.

It's a digital zoom: the page enlarges the picture the camera sends, so you don't get more detail than the camera gives you.

docs.title: Tool
docs.text:
Moving and extruding, like Fluidd's Tool card.

  • Arrows move X, Y and Z by the distance picked under them. Home buttons home all axes, X and Y, X, Y or Z.
  • Position fields show where the toolhead is. Type a value to move there; the button next to them switches between absolute and relative moves.
  • Extrude length and speed, then Retract or Extrude. The line under them shows how much filament that is and how fast.
  • Z offset with its step sizes, and a button to save it.
  • Speed, Flow, Pressure advance and Smooth time sliders. The arrow next to each puts it back to the printer's own value.
  • FORCE_MOVE only shows when [force_move] is in your config. It asks before turning it on.
  • Tools has Load filament, Unload filament, Clean nozzle, Park toolhead and calibration commands.
  • Motors off shows when the printer is ready and homed. It asks first, and the axes need homing again after.

Jog distances, speeds and inverted axes are in Settings → Tool.

docs.title: Macros
docs.text:
The macros panel shows each of your printer's macros as a button, in groups.

  • Click a macro to run it. A macro that takes values has a small arrow next to it: click the arrow to open a box with a field for each value, then Send. The name button runs it without values.
  • Hide some… shows an × on each button so you can hide the ones you never use. Show hidden brings them back.
  • The gear on a group's heading opens Organize, where you put macros in groups you name, such as Calibration or Camera. The arrow on the heading folds the group. Macros without a group are under Uncategorized.
  • Suggest groups (in Organize) sorts macros that aren't in a group yet, by their names, into Print, Calibration, Motion, Filament, Temperature, Camera, Lights and System. Macros that share a first word, such as MMU_LOAD and MMU_UNLOAD, go in a group named after it. Macros you've already grouped stay where they are.
  • Lock (in Organize) greys a macro out while a print is running or paused. An unlocked macro still asks you to confirm when you run it during a print.

Groups, locks and hidden macros are saved in your browser, for each printer.

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text:
The Jobs panel lists the G-code files on the printer, like Fluidd's Jobs card.

  • Click a column heading to sort by name, last printed, modified or size. The column button picks which columns show.
  • Click a file for its menu: Print, Add to Queue, Preheat, Edit or View, Preview G-code, Download, Rename, Duplicate, Create zip, Refresh metadata and Remove (some only show for files they apply to). Click a folder to open it.
  • The toolbar has thumbnail size, columns, go to file, a filter, + to upload or make a folder, refresh, and a search box.

docs.title: Job queue
docs.text:
The queue panel lines up prints to run one after another. Add files with Add to Queue in the Jobs panel. For each file you can set how many copies to print (− and +), move it to the front with ↑ Next, or remove it. Resume and Pause control when the next job starts.

Under the list it adds up the queue: Filament (metres and grams), Print time and ETA, the time the whole queue should finish. If a print is running, the ETA includes what's left of it. If some files have no estimate in them, a note says how many.

On the Jobs tab the queue only shows when something is queued.

docs.title: G-code preview
docs.text:
Shows a print file layer by layer, in 2D or 3D.

  • Load current file loads the file that's printing; the menu next to it picks any file.
  • Layer and Progress sliders step through the layers and through one layer. Reset file clears it.
  • The buttons over the picture turn on and off: follow the print, the previous, current and next layer, moves, extrusions, and objects.
  • Objects draws each object of the print on the bed, if your slicer labels objects and [exclude_object] is in your config. While printing, click an object's × to skip it for the rest of the print. It asks first.

docs.title: Tune
docs.text:
• Bed Mesh draws the mesh. Calibrate probes a new one. Switch between the mesh and the probed points, flat or 3D, and the grid lines.
  • Bed Mesh Controls lists your saved profiles: load or remove one, Save as…, Clear, and Manual probe.
  • End Stops shows whether each end stop is open or triggered. Press the refresh button to check again.
  • Runout Sensors shows whether filament is detected, with a switch to turn each sensor on or off.
  • Beacon only shows on a printer with a Beacon probe: load, save or remove models, and Calibrate.

A manual probe (from Manual probe or Z calibration) opens a box where you step the nozzle down until a sheet of paper just drags, then Accept.

Bed screws opens its own box: turn the screw it names, then press Adjusted, or Accept when it's right. Abort stops.

docs.title: MMU and AMS
docs.text: The MMU / AMS panel shows the filament slots, which one is loaded, and lets you load and unload (Happy Hare, AFC, Bambu AMS). With AFC (Box Turtle, Night Owl…) each unit shows its lanes, with colour, material and how much is left; clicking a lane loads it. On a Creality K2 it shows the CFS units and their slots, with colours and humidity; load and unload stay on the printer.

docs.title: Console
docs.text:
Type G-code and press Send.

  • ↑ / ↓ go through the commands you've sent. Tab completes a command or macro name.
  • Start typing to get suggestions for every command and macro Klipper knows.
  • The toolbar has search, filters (hide lines you don't care about, like temperature reports), clear, and a button that puts the newest lines at the top instead of the bottom.
  • ? next to the title shows the console's keys when you hover over it.
  • Type help to open a searchable list of every command.
  • Click a line you sent to put it back in the box.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Statistics adds up the printer's history: total jobs, longest job, total and average time, print time and filament. The cog shows time in days and length in kilometres; the bin resets the statistics (the list stays).
  • History lists every print. Search it, pick columns, Load all, Remove all (it asks first), download it as CSV, open Charts and Maintenance reminders, and click a print for its details, notes and Reprint.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Config files lists the printer's config folder. The menu at the top switches to Config examples or Docs, which you can only view.

  • Click a file to open it in the editor. Images open in a viewer.
  • Right-click a file or folder for Edit, Rename, Duplicate, Download, Create zip and Delete. Delete asks first.
  • + Add makes a new file or folder, or uploads files or a whole folder. The toolbar also has a search box, Filter, Go to file and refresh. You can also drag files onto the list, and drag a file onto a folder to move it.
  • Tick several files to zip or delete them together.

docs.title: The editor
docs.text:
The editor opens full screen, with the file's name at the top and ● unsaved when you have changes.

  • Outline lists every [section] in the file; click one to jump to it. Turn it off in the panel's settings.
  • The minimap on the right shows the whole file shrunk down. Click it to jump, or drag the grey band to scroll.
  • Find (Ctrl+F) searches the file, with Replace and All to replace the matches, and Aa to match capitals.
  • Docs: [section] opens Klipper's Config Reference for the section the cursor is in.
  • Save (Ctrl+S) saves the file. Save & restart saves it and restarts Klipper, or Moonraker for Moonraker's files. It asks first and is off while printing.
  • Tab puts in two spaces. Esc or × closes the editor, and asks first if you have unsaved changes.

The outline and the minimap are hidden on small screens.

docs.title: System
docs.text:
• System Overview shows the printer's computer (hostname, OS, CPU, memory, network) with Restart Klipper, Firmware Restart and the log downloads. Its buttons open Devices (serial, USB, CAN and camera IDs) and roll the logs over.
  • SD Card Information and Disk Information (used and free space for each folder).
  • Moonraker Database backs up and restores Moonraker's database, which holds your print history, spools and saved settings. Restoring replaces everything, so it asks first, and it's off while printing. Compact Database shrinks the file.
  • System Utilization has small charts of system load, memory, Klipper, Moonraker and each MCU. They fill in while the page is open.
  • MCU Information shows each board's chip, speed and firmware version.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: General, Theme, Notifications, AI Detection, Console, File Browser, Macros, Cameras, Plate Check, Tool, Thermal Presets, Gcode Preview, Updates, Other Card Options, Machine, Devices and About, plus every panel's own options in one place.

docs.title: Plate check
docs.text:
Warns you before printing on top of something left on the bed.

  1. Clear the bed, then press Take it now under Settings → Plate Check to save the empty-bed picture.
  2. When you start a print from Printer Buddy, the start box compares the camera with that picture and says whether the bed looks empty. You can still print anyway.

Sensitivity sets how much has to change. Test now checks it straight away. It only checks prints started from Printer Buddy, needs a camera that sees the bed, and needs a new picture if the camera or light changes a lot.

docs.title: Top bar
docs.text:
Button What it does Save config Only shows when Klipper has unsaved changes — see below Theme Switches between auto (follows your system), light and dark Edit layout Add, move and remove panels and tabs E-Stop Stops the printer immediately ☰ The printer drawer: restarts, host power, services

Pause and Cancel are on the Printer Status panel, at the top of the Dashboard.

docs.title: Errors and warnings
docs.text:
When Klipper isn't ready, a Klippy card at the top of the page shows its state (for example Klippy: shutdown), Klipper's own message in red, and buttons for Restart Klipper, Firmware Restart and the klippy.log and moonraker.log downloads.

When there are warnings — deprecated config options, a Moonraker plugin that failed to start, or on a Bambu printer its own notices (like "The AMS filament ran out") — they're listed in yellow on the same card.

When Printer Buddy can't reach the printer at all, the page shows the printer's address and No Moonraker connection, with Force refresh. Printer Buddy keeps trying in the background.

A Bambu printer's errors show in words, such as "The nozzle is clogged. (0300_4006)", instead of a bare number.

docs.title: Save config
docs.text: After a calibration, bed mesh, offset or anything else Klipper hasn't saved yet, an orange Save config button appears. Click it to see exactly what will be written to printer.cfg, then Save config & restart (runs SAVE_CONFIG, which restarts Klipper). It's disabled while printing.

docs.title: Remote access
docs.text: By default Printer Buddy only works on your home network. Remote access lets you check a printer from anywhere with a share link.

docs.title: Turning it on
docs.text:
Pick Remote access = on in 2) Change setup and go back. The installer then installs a secure tunnel (cloudflared), registers it and starts it.

Turn it off again and the installer asks whether to remove the tunnel. Share links stop working from outside once it's removed.

docs.title: Share links
docs.text:
Share a printer's view with someone else. Links look like:

https://www.printerbuddy.stream/share/user/<your id>/...

To make one, open the menu on a printer's card on the home page and choose Share. It only shows when remote access is on. Pick how long the link works:

  • 1 hour, 1 day or 7 days
  • until the print ends — only offered while a print is running. The link turns itself off when the print finishes, is cancelled or fails.
  • until I turn it off

Untick Chat if you want a link with no chat box at all. Then Create link, and Copy it. The list shows each link and when it stops working, and Turn off ends one straight away.

The people you send it to see the printer's camera, progress, time left, layer and temperatures. They can't control anything. On the page, the full screen button in the corner of the camera fills the screen (double-click does the same) and the same button leaves it.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
Everyone watching a printer through a share link can chat. The page has a Chat button next to the printer's name: click it to open the chat box, and click it again to close it. Each viewer types a name (it's remembered in their browser) and a message, and everyone watching that printer sees it, whichever of your links they used.

You see the same chat in the Share window in Printer Buddy and can write in it as Owner. Clear chat empties it for everyone. The Allow chat tickbox there switches chat on or off for that printer: it's on by default, and turning it off hides the Chat button on every share link for that printer and clears the chat.

  • A link made with Chat unticked never shows the chat button, and the list marks it "no chat".
  • Messages are plain text, up to 300 characters, one every 2 seconds per viewer.
  • The last 100 messages are kept in memory. They're gone when Printer Buddy restarts.
  • A link that's turned off or has expired loses the chat too.

docs.title: Push notifications
docs.text:
Open Alerts and blocked words in the chat part of the Share window and pick Notify me with a push. It uses the notification service you set up in Settings.

  • Never: chat stays quiet. You only see it when you open the window.
  • Only when a viewer flags the print (the default).
  • For every message: at most one push every 20 seconds, saying how many more came in.

docs.title: Flag button
docs.text: Next to Send, viewers have a Flag button for when they spot something the AI missed. It asks them to confirm, then sends you a push with a camera picture, using whatever they typed (up to 100 characters) as the reason. The flag also shows in the chat. Flags always push unless alerts are set to Never. A viewer can flag once a minute, and a printer takes at most 5 flags in 10 minutes.

docs.title: Blocked words
docs.text:
The same section has a list of words that aren't allowed, one per line. A message or name containing one is refused and the viewer is told so, and they can't send or flag anything for 10 seconds. You see the attempt in your chat window, in grey, with the name and what they typed. Other viewers never see it, and you aren't sent a push for it. It's saved in chat-blocklist.txt next to the database, so you can edit that file instead if you prefer. On top of your list, a built-in list of common swear words, insults and slurs is blocked. Untick Also block the built-in list of swear words and slurs to turn it off. Changes to the alerts and the word list take effect when you press Save. It can't catch every spelling, and it only blocks whole words, so ordinary words like "class" or "assist" are fine.

  • word blocks that whole word only, two words blocks the phrase.
  • word* blocks any word that starts with it, *word any word that ends with it, and *word* blocks it anywhere, even inside other words.
  • Capitals, accents, look-alikes (1 for i, 0 for o, @ for a) and spaces between letters (b a d) are caught.

docs.title: Who can see what
docs.text: There's no login. Each share link has its own long, secret code, and anyone with the link can see that printer, so only send it to people you trust. Links can be set to expire, and Turn off stops a link straight away.

docs.title: Turning it on
docs.text: Pick Video = timelapse in the installer. It installs ffmpeg, which makes the videos.

docs.title: How it records
docs.text:
Setting Choices Default Take a picture every layer, or every few seconds every layer every (every few seconds) 5, 10 or 30 seconds between pictures 10 s Video speed 15, 25 or 30 frames per second 25 fps Keep the last 5, 10, 20, 50 or 100 timelapses per printer 20

A timelapse starts with the print and the video is made when it ends. Prints with fewer than two frames don't make a video.

Every layer uses the layer number your slicer puts in the file. If the file doesn't have one, Printer Buddy works the layer out from the nozzle height, and a quick Z-hop doesn't count as a new layer.

If Printer Buddy restarts during a print, that print's timelapse is lost.

docs.title: Finding your videos
docs.text:
Open the printer's Timelapse tab. It has three panels:

  • Timelapses — your videos, to watch, download or delete. They're stored in Printer Buddy's data/ folder.
  • Timelapse Status — whether a timelapse is recording now, and how many pictures it has so far.
  • Timelapse Settings — when to take a picture, the video speed and how many to keep, from the table above. Changes apply to all printers from the next print.
